# Finance Planner — llms.txt

> AI assistants: this file is the entry point for answering retirement
> questions with this repo's engines. The full guide is
> assistant-api/README.md; this file carries the summary and one worked
> example so a single link is enough to start.

## What the adapter is

A stateless, read-only MCP server (`assistant-api/`) over the Finance
Planner's own retirement engines. Every call carries its complete
scenario in dollars — balances, spending, ages, Social Security — and
nothing is saved, read from a database, or remembered between calls.
Pricing uses the 2026 tax-law tables unless `taxYear` says 2025.

## Where it lives

- Server + tools: `assistant-api/` (`src/server.ts`, `src/tools.ts`)
- Full guide: `assistant-api/README.md`
- Client config: `assistant-api/mcp.json` (copy the `mcpServers` block)
- Registry metadata (not published): `assistant-api/server.json`

## The 8 tools (one line each)

- `retirement_calculate` — can the money last to the end age? Ending balance + year-by-year table + historical cross-check.
- `retirement_monte_carlo` — how likely is the plan to succeed? Success rate (0–1) + p10/p50/p90 outcomes.
- `retirement_max_spending` — highest sustainable monthly spending at 85% Monte Carlo success.
- `retirement_compare_strategies` — which account to spend from first? Taxable-first vs pre-tax-first vs Roth-first, tax-aware.
- `retirement_roth_conversion` — convert to Roth? Do Nothing vs Fill 12% vs Fill 22% vs Fill 22% capped at IRMAA Tier 1.
- `retirement_work_years` — retire at which age? Tax-aware comparison across `compareAges`; add `salaryAnnual` for the work-years leg.
- `retirement_tax_year` — one year's federal/state tax, ACA credit, and IRMAA for a published law year (2025 or 2026 today).
- `retirement_describe_capabilities` — no inputs; returns the machine-readable guide to all of the above.

## Quick-start

Local (zero-config, localhost only, no token needed):

```sh
cd assistant-api && bun run start   # listens on http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp
```

Remote (one command from the repo root; needs a bearer token):

```sh
ASSISTANT_API_TOKEN=<a-long-random-token> assistant-api/deploy.sh
```

No public HTTPS endpoint is live yet — deployment is the reader's step.
Remote calls need `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request.

## Minimal worked example

Question: "Can I retire at 58?" (fictional household: pre-tax
$1,250,000; taxable $2,100,000; Roth $375,000; HSA $62,000; spending
$9,500/mo; ages 54/52; Social Security $36,000/yr at 67, spouse
$18,000/yr at 67; taxable basis 72%; retire 58; end age 95)

Tool call:

```json
{
  "name": "retirement_calculate",
  "arguments": {
    "pretax": 1250000, "taxable": 2100000, "roth": 375000, "hsa": 62000,
    "monthlySpending": 9500, "currentAge": 54, "spouseAge": 52,
    "retirementAge": 58, "endAge": 95,
    "socialSecurityAnnual": 36000, "socialSecurityStartAge": 67,
    "spouseSocialSecurityAnnual": 18000, "spouseSocialSecurityStartAge": 67,
    "taxableBasisPct": 72, "taxYear": 2026
  }
}
```

Result (key figures): `neverRunsOut: true`, ending balance
$43,901,094.30 at age 95, historical never-out rate 100%.

Six inputs are always required: `pretax`, `taxable`, `roth`, `hsa`,
`monthlySpending`, `currentAge` (explicit 0 counts). Everything else
has a documented default; missing essentials return a structured
`missing_input` error with a plain-language question per field — ask
the user those questions, don't guess.

## What it cannot do

- No saved data: it never reads the app database, saved records, or
  the fictional sample household. The app's own saved plans are
  answered through the app, not this server.
- Tax years 2025/2026 only (the published law years); no public endpoint live yet; the
  work-years leg with a spouse Social Security benefit needs more
  than 6 GB (run it without the spouse benefit, or wait for a bigger
  host). Full list: `assistant-api/README.md`, "Known limitations".

## The full doc

There is no `llms-full.txt` — `assistant-api/README.md` is the full
documentation: architecture, tool inventory, assumptions table,
security model, test commands, and four worked conversation
transcripts.
